comparePanel.floodIntro: The simulation forecasts flood levels based on the rainfall parameters you selected. The metrics below reflect conditions before and after the scenario.
comparePanel.floodRiskBeforeDesc: Overall flood risk score (0–100%) before the scenario, from observed rainfall, terrain sensitivity (DEM), imperviousness (WorldCover) and drainage capacity.
comparePanel.affectedAreasDesc: Number of flooded zones before → after the scenario. An increase means heavier rain floods more places.
comparePanel.heatIntro: Results analyze the Urban Heat Island (UHI) effect. Effective temperature includes effects of building density, greenery and traffic.
comparePanel.tempDeltaDesc: Change in effective temperature vs baseline. Negative values (green) are good — the scenario cools the city.
comparePanel.floodRiskImpactDesc: High temperatures increase evaporation and alter rain cycles, indirectly affecting flood risk. Shows level before → after.
comparePanel.aqiIntro: Simulation of traffic, greenery and rain impact on AQI. Negative values mean air quality improvement.
comparePanel.aqiDeltaDesc: Change in AQI when applying the scenario. Lower AQI (green) means cleaner air. Scale: 0–50 Good | 51–100 Moderate | 101–150 Sensitive | >150 Unhealthy.
comparePanel.tempDeltaAqiDesc: Temperature and AQI are linked: higher temperatures promote ground-level ozone formation and raise AQI. Reducing traffic and adding greenery lowers both.

maturity.title: Model maturity (Algorithm 1)
maturity.subtitle: Stage S1 → S2 → S3 per hazard, re-evaluated on stored data
maturity.purpose: Each hazard runs on published coefficients (S1) until enough local observations exist to self-calibrate (S2) or train a dedicated model (S3); if the data no longer supports a stage, the model demotes back to S1 instead of degrading silently.

flood.S2: re-fits w₁–w₄ on an observed inundation-depth series
flood.S3: trained on archived data, no fixed formula

heat.S2: re-fits α, u on a land-surface temperature series (Landsat LST)
heat.S3: trained on archived data, no fixed formula

aqi.S2: γ_w, γ_p re-estimated by OLS regression on local observations (below)
aqi.S3: trained on archived data, no fixed formula

R-FLOOD-01.title: Severe flood risk
R-FLOOD-01.message: Severe flood risk at {name}: risk score {riskPct}%, rainfall {rainfall}mm/h above the danger threshold.
actions: Avoid travelling through low-lying areas
Do not drive into flooded roads
Move vehicles to higher ground or a safe location
Follow emergency notices from local authorities
Prepare an emergency bag in case of evacuation

R-FLOOD-02.title: Possible flooding in the next 2 hours
R-FLOOD-02.message: High chance of flooding within the next 2h at {name}. Risk score: {riskPct}%.
actions: Limit travel during peak rain hours
Choose routes avoiding flood-prone areas
Check the flood forecast before heading out
Schedule trips earlier than usual

R-FLOOD-03.title: Monitor rainfall conditions
R-FLOOD-03.message: Monitor rainfall at {name} (risk score {riskPct}%) — light flooding possible if rain continues.
actions: Check the weather before going out
Avoid parking in low-lying areas
Keep a raincoat and boots ready

R-COMB-01.title: Flooding and air pollution at once
R-COMB-01.message: Double hazard at {name}: high flood risk ({riskPct}%) combined with AQI {aqi} nearby. Minimize going outside.
actions: Stay indoors with windows closed
Follow emergency notices from local authorities
Prepare drinking water and food supplies
Keep your phone fully charged
Contact family about your situation

R-AQI-01.title: Very poor air quality
R-AQI-01.message: Very poor air quality at {name} (AQI {aqi}). Avoid going outside except for emergencies.
actions: Stay indoors with windows closed
Use an air purifier
Avoid outdoor exercise
Wear an N95 mask if you must go outside
Children, the elderly and people with respiratory conditions should take extra care

R-AQI-02.title: Unhealthy AQI level
R-AQI-02.message: AQI at {name} is at an unhealthy level ({aqi}). Wear an N95 mask outdoors.
actions: Wear an N95 or KN95 mask
Limit strenuous outdoor activity
Sensitive groups should stay indoors
Drink plenty of water

R-AQI-03.title: AQI unhealthy for sensitive groups
R-AQI-03.message: AQI at {name} is {aqi}. Sensitive groups should limit outdoor activity.
actions: Wear a mask for prolonged time outside
Avoid intense outdoor exercise

R-HEAT-01.title: Extreme heat
R-HEAT-01.message: Extreme heat at {name} — effective temperature {temp}°C. High risk of heatstroke.
actions: Avoid going out between 10:00-16:00
Drink at least 3 litres of water a day
Wear light-coloured, breathable clothing
Never leave children or the elderly in a car
Know the signs of heatstroke: dizziness, nausea

R-HEAT-02.title: High temperature, stay hydrated
R-HEAT-02.message: Effective temperature at {name} is high ({temp}°C). Drink enough water and avoid direct sun.
actions: Drink at least 2 litres of water a day
Wear a hat and protective clothing
Rest in the shade

R-NORM-00.title: Normal conditions
R-NORM-00.message: Weather and air quality are within safe limits across all spatial units.
actions: Continue routine monitoring
